chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fudayla ibn Ayyub and Ibn Abi Umayr and Hammad from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Go to the standing place of Gabriel (peace be upon him), which is under the be upon him), and it is beneath the gutter, for it was his standing place when he sought permission from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Then say: I ask you, O Generous, O Noble, O Close, O Distant, to send blessings upon Muhammad and his family, and I ask you to return my favor."
He said, "And that is a standing place where a menstruating woman who faces the qibla does not supplicate with the supplication of blood except that she sees purity, if God wills."

And the Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) mentioned in the Risala that you come to Al-Rawdah and visit Fatimah (peace be upon her) because she is buried there. And our companions have differed regarding the location of her grave: some of them said that she was buried in Al-Baqi', and some of them said that she was buried in Al-Rawdah, and some of them said that she was buried in her house. And when the Banu Umayya (may God curse them) added to the mosque, it became part of the mosque.
And these two narrations are similar, and the best in my opinion is that the person visits both places, for that will not harm him and he will acquire great reward through it.
As for whoever said that she was buried in Al-Baqi', that is far from the truth.
And what has been narrated regarding the virtue of visiting her is more than can be counted, and he has narrated.
ai.seo_question: Where is Fatimah's grave located and what is the supplication to recite at Gabriel's standing place?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the spiritual significance of the *Maqam Jibril* beneath the mosque's gutter, where the Angel Gabriel sought permission to enter, offering a specific supplication for divine favor. It further addresses the scholarly debate regarding the burial site of Fatimah al-Zahra (peace be upon her), with Shaykh al-Tusi favoring the *Rawdah* or her house over Al-Baqi' to maximize the reward of visitation (*Ziyarah*).
